description: Konnektoren (connectors) are words and phrases that link clauses and sentences. They include coordinating conjunctions (und, aber, oder, denn, sondern), subordinating conjunctions (weil, obwohl, damit, bevor), adverbial connectors (deshalb, trotzdem, jednak, außerdem), and two-part connectors (einerseits/andererseits, zwar/aber, sowohl/als auch). B2 level requires precision in choosing the semantically correct connector and mastering the word order effects each type triggers.
tips: Subordinating conjunctions (weil, obwohl, damit, bevor, nachdem, während) → verb goes to the END of the clause (verb-final). Coordinating conjunctions (und, aber, oder, denn, sondern) → normal word order in the following clause.
Adverbial connectors (deshalb, daher, trotzdem, allerdings, dennoch, außerdem, dabei) → trigger INVERSION (verb before subject) when starting a main clause.
Weil vs Denn: both express reason, but 'weil' is subordinating (verb-final) and 'denn' is coordinating (normal word order).
Obwohl vs Aber: 'obwohl' (although) is subordinating (verb-final); 'aber' (but) is coordinating (normal order). Don't confuse: obwohl + verb-final, aber + normal order.
Sodass (so that) → consecutive clause expressing result/consequence, verb-final. Damit (in order that) → purpose clause, verb-final, subject in both clauses usually same.
Sondern: only used AFTER a negation to correct/contrast. Nicht A, sondern B. 'Aber' expresses simple contrast without requiring prior negation.
Zwar … aber (it's true that … but) → two-part concessive connector. Zwar can start a main clause (verb follows) or be inside a clause (verb stays at end).
Einerseits … andererseits → two-part connector for contrasting aspects. Triggers inversion when starting a clause.
Deshalb/daher → express consequence/result (therefore). Trigger inversion. Weill → express reason. Don't mix up: wenn/Da + consequence = deshalb.
Two-part connectors: sowohl … als auch (both … and), weder … noch (neither … nor), entweder … oder (either … or) — all are coordinating and maintain normal word order in the following clause.

questions.questionText: Er hat viel gearbeitet, ____ er hat die Prüfung nicht bestanden.
questions.explanation: 'Trotzdem' is an adverbial connector (Konjunktionaladverb) that causes inversion: subject follows the verb. After a comma it starts a new main clause: 'er hat … → trotzdem hat er …'. However, when placed after the comma mid-sentence without inversion as here, 'trotzdem' fits. 'Obwohl' is a subordinating conjunction requiring verb-final word order and cannot connect two main clauses this way.

questions.questionText: Ich lerne Deutsch, ____ ich in Deutschland studieren möchte.
questions.explanation: 'Weil' is a subordinating conjunction (Subjunktor) — verb goes to the end of the clause. 'Denn' is a coordinating conjunction that does NOT change word order, but the sentence structure here (comma + clause with modal) fits 'weil' better. 'Deshalb/daher' are adverbial connectors meaning 'therefore' — they express result, not reason.

questions.questionText: Sie ist krank, ____ kommt sie heute nicht ins Büro.
questions.explanation: 'Deshalb' (therefore/that's why) is an adverbial connector expressing consequence. It triggers inversion: 'deshalb kommt sie …'. The reason is stated first (she is ill), then the result follows. 'Weil' would require verb-final order and introduces a reason clause, not a result clause.

questions.questionText: Wir können ins Kino gehen ____ zu Hause einen Film schauen.
questions.explanation: 'Oder' (or) connects two alternatives. 'Sondern' is used after a negation to contrast (not A but rather B). 'Aber/doch' express contrast, not alternation. Here no negation precedes, so 'sondern' is ruled out.

questions.questionText: Er ist nicht müde, ____ er will einfach nicht aufstehen.
questions.explanation: 'Sondern' follows a negation ('nicht müde') to introduce a contrasting correction: not A, but rather B. 'Aber' also expresses contrast but without the correction nuance and does not require prior negation. This 'nicht … sondern' structure is a core B2 connector distinction.

questions.questionText: Das Meeting dauert lange, ____ wir können pünktlich gehen.
questions.explanation: 'Aber' (but) is a coordinating conjunction expressing contrast without inversion — it sits between two main clauses and word order in the second clause stays normal (subject-verb). 'Sondern' requires prior negation, which is absent here.

questions.questionText: Ich trinke keinen Kaffee, ____ ich trinke lieber Tee.
questions.explanation: After 'keinen Kaffee' (negation with 'kein-'), 'sondern' introduces the corrective alternative: not coffee, but rather tea. This is the classic 'nicht/kein … sondern' construction. 'Aber' could express contrast but lacks the corrective replacement meaning.

questions.questionText: Das Projekt wurde abgeschlossen, ____ wurden neue Herausforderungen sichtbar.
questions.explanation: 'Dabei' as an adverbial connector means 'in the process / at the same time'. It triggers inversion and adds a simultaneous or accompanying circumstance: while completing the project, new challenges became visible. This nuanced use of 'dabei' is typical of B2 written registers.

questions.questionText: ____ er intensiv trainierte, verbesserte sich seine Leistung kaum.
questions.explanation: 'Obwohl' (although) introduces a concessive clause — the training didn't produce the expected improvement, creating a contrast. Verb goes to the end: 'obwohl er … trainierte'. When the subordinate clause leads, the main clause begins with the verb (inversion): 'verbesserte sich seine Leistung'.

questions.questionText: Sie sprach sehr leise, ____ ihre Zuhörer sie kaum verstehen konnten.
questions.explanation: 'Sodass' (so that / with the result that) introduces a consecutive clause describing an unintended consequence. Verb goes to the end. Contrast with 'damit' (in order that), which expresses an intended purpose with a different subject. Here the quiet speaking was not intentional — it resulted in listeners struggling.

questions.questionText: Er hat die Stelle bekommen, ____ er keine Berufserfahrung hatte.
questions.explanation: 'Obwohl' (although/even though) introduces a concessive subordinate clause. Getting the job despite lacking experience is the unexpected concession. 'Weil' would mean because of lacking experience — the opposite logical relationship.

questions.questionText: Wir müssen früh aufbrechen, ____ wir den letzten Zug noch erwischen.
questions.explanation: 'Damit' (so that / in order that) expresses purpose when the subjects of the two clauses differ or the action is intentional. Here: leaving early is intentional with the goal of catching the train. 'Sodass' would express an unintended consequence, not a planned goal.

questions.questionText: Einerseits ist die Stelle gut bezahlt, ____ sind die Arbeitsbedingungen sehr belastend.
questions.explanation: 'Einerseits … andererseits' (on one hand … on the other hand) is a two-part connector presenting two contrasting aspects. It is an adverbial connector triggering inversion: 'andererseits sind die Arbeitsbedingungen …'. This paired structure is essential B2 argumentation vocabulary.

questions.questionText: Das Angebot klingt verlockend. ____ sollte man das Kleingedruckte sorgfältig lesen.
questions.explanation: 'Dennoch' (nevertheless/nonetheless) is an adverbial connector expressing concession between two independent sentences. It triggers inversion: 'Dennoch sollte man …'. It is more formal than 'trotzdem' and typical of written B2 argumentation. 'Obwohl' cannot start an independent main clause.

questions.questionText: ____ die Kosten gestiegen sind, ____ hat die Nachfrage nicht nachgelassen.
questions.explanation: 'Zwar … aber' (it's true that … but) is a two-part connector for concessive contrast within connected clauses. 'Zwar' can begin a main clause or subordinate clause; 'aber' begins the contrasting main clause. Word order after 'zwar' in first position: verb follows immediately (inversion). A very common B2 written register structure.

questions.questionText: Das neue System ist effizienter. ____ sind die Schulungskosten erheblich gestiegen, ____ viele Mitarbeiter überfordert wirken.
questions.explanation: 'Allerdings' (however/admittedly) is a formal adverbial connector signalling a limiting concession — it triggers inversion. 'Sodass' then introduces the consecutive result clause (costs rose, resulting in employees seeming overwhelmed). This two-connector chain (concession → consequence) is a hallmark of complex B2 argumentative writing.

questions.questionText: Die Verhandlungen scheiterten, ____ beide Parteien monatelang verhandelt hatten, ____ man zunächst Einigkeit erwartet hatte.
questions.explanation: 'Obwohl' introduces the concessive subordinate clause (despite months of negotiation). 'Und' then adds a second parallel subordinate clause ('und man … erwartet hatte') — two subordinate clauses joined by 'und' sharing the same matrix clause. This stacked subordinate clause structure is B2+ syntactic complexity.

questions.questionText: Der Bericht zeigt, dass ____ die Emissionen gesunken sind, ____ der Gesamtausstoß weiterhin zu hoch bleibt.
questions.explanation: 'Zwar … aber' inside a 'dass'-clause: 'dass zwar … gesunken sind, aber … bleibt'. Both clauses are embedded under 'dass', making this a complex nested structure. 'Zwar' does not trigger inversion when inside a subordinate clause — verb stays at the end of each clause. This is an advanced B2+ written register pattern.

questions.questionText: Er arbeitet sehr hart. ____ gelingt es ihm nicht, die Erwartungen seiner Vorgesetzten zu erfüllen, ____ er beginnt, an sich zu zweifeln.
questions.explanation: 'Dennoch' (nevertheless) begins the second sentence with inversion, expressing that despite hard work, expectations are not met. 'Sodass' then introduces the resulting psychological consequence (he begins to doubt himself). This chain — concession (dennoch) → result (sodass) — across sentence boundaries is a sophisticated B2 connector pattern.

questions.questionText: Die Reform wurde verabschiedet, ____ zahlreiche Experten gewarnt hatten, ____ sie in der Praxis kaum umsetzbar sei.
questions.explanation: 'Obwohl' introduces the concessive clause; within that clause, a further subordinate 'dass'-clause reports the content of the experts' warning: 'obwohl … gewarnt hatten, dass sie … sei'. Note 'sei' = Konjunktiv I in indirect speech inside the embedded clause. This double embedding (obwohl + dass + K-I) represents the highest B2 syntactic complexity.

questions.questionText: Wir müssen die Produktionskosten drastisch senken, ____ wird das Unternehmen Ende des Jahres Insolvenz anmelden müssen.
questions.explanation: The context requires a connector meaning 'otherwise' to show the negative consequence of not acting. 'Andernfalls' is a conjunctive adverb that triggers inversion (verb 'wird' comes directly after it).

questions.questionText: ____ mehr Fachkräfte wir für dieses anspruchsvolle IT-Projekt einstellen, ____ schneller können wir die Software auf den Markt bringen.
questions.explanation: 'JE... umso' (or 'je... desto') is a proportional connector. 'Je' introduces the subordinate clause (verb at the end), and 'umso/desto' introduces the main clause, triggering immediate verb inversion ('können wir').

questions.questionText: Der neue Mitarbeiter hat die schwierige Aufgabe ohne jede Hilfe gelöst, ____ der Abteilungsleiter ihm Unterstützung versprochen hatte.
questions.explanation: The clause requires a subordinating concession connector ('although') because the verb 'hatte' sits at the very end. 'Obgleich' is a higher-level synonym of 'obwohl'. 'Trotzdem' would mean 'nevertheless' and require main clause word order.

questions.questionText: Er hat nicht einmal genug Geld für die monatliche Miete, ____ für eine zweiwöchige Urlaubsreise nach Japan.
questions.explanation: The idiomatic expression 'geschweige denn' means 'let alone' or 'not to mention'. It is used after a negative statement to emphasize that the next option is even more impossible.

questions.questionText: Die Geschäftsführung hat die Budgets gekürzt. ____ müssen wir alle geplanten Marketingkampagnen vorerst stoppen.
questions.explanation: The sentence requires a conjunctive adverb meaning 'as a result / consequently'. 'Infolgedessen' occupies position 1, followed directly by the conjugated verb 'müssen'. 'Infolge' is a preposition requiring a noun in the genitive, and 'sodass' introduces a subordinate clause.

questions.questionText: Die Verhandlungen waren äußerst zäh, ____ konnte am späten Abend doch noch eine Einigung erzielt werden.
questions.explanation: 'Gleichwohl' is an advanced, formal C1/B2 concessive adverb meaning 'nevertheless / yet'. It fits perfectly because it contrasts the tough negotiations with the eventual success and triggers inversion ('konnte... eine Einigung erzielt werden').

questions.questionText: Sie hat die anspruchsvolle B2-Prüfung fehlerfrei bestanden, ____ sie sich kaum darauf vorbereitet hatte.
questions.explanation: 'Obschon' is a formal subordinating conjunction meaning 'although' (synonym to 'obwohl' / 'obgleich'). It introduces a subordinate clause with the verb 'hatte' at the end. 'Wohingegen' is used for direct contrast ('whereas').

questions.questionText: ____ wir pünktlich Feierabend machen können, müssen alle Berichte bis 15:00 Uhr vollständig vorliegen.
questions.explanation: This is a final (purpose) clause with its verb 'können' at the end. Because the subject 'wir' is explicitly named, 'um... zu' cannot be used. 'Damit' is the correct subordinating conjunction.

questions.questionText: Das Gesetz wurde gestern im Bundestag beschlossen und tritt ____ am ersten Januar des kommenden Jahres in Kraft.
questions.explanation: 'Demnach' is a logical connector meaning 'accordingly / therefore / thus'. It functions here as an adverb within the main clause. 'Nachdem' is temporal and requires a subordinate verb position.

questions.questionText: Wir sollten den Vertrag jetzt unterschreiben, ____ wir es später bereuen, diese einmalige Chance verpasst zu haben.
questions.explanation: The idiomatic fixed expression 'nicht dass' + subordinate clause is used here in the colloquial/expressive sense of 'lest' or 'for fear that' (...lest we regret it later). It functions as a warning connector.

questions.questionText: Die Sanierung des alten Gebäudes ist ____ extrem kostspielig, ____ sie bringt langfristig eine enorme Energieeinsparung.
questions.explanation: The sentence weighs a negative point (expensive) against a positive point (energy saving). The concessive connector pair 'zwar... aber' (indeed... but) perfectly matches this counter-balancing context.

questions.questionText: Die ältere Dame überquerte die viel befahrene Straße, ____ auf den dichten Berufsverkehr zu achten.
questions.explanation: This requires an infinitive clause structure because of 'zu achten' at the end. 'Ohne... zu' translates to 'without doing something'. Since the underlying subject is the same as the main clause, 'ohne dass' (subordinate clause) is incorrect.

questions.questionText: Die Bundesstraße muss komplett gesperrt werden, ____ die Schäden am Asphalt repariert werden können.
questions.explanation: This expresses a consecutive outcome (so that / with the result that). 'Sodass' introduces the subordinate clause containing the result of the road closure.

questions.questionText: Der Verdächtige schwieg während der gesamten Vernehmung, ____ seine Schuld quasi einzugestehen.
questions.explanation: In this specific stylistic context, 'um... zu' acts not as a goal, but as a consecutive infinitive clause expressing an unintended or logical outcome ('..., thereby practically admitting his guilt').

questions.questionText: Man kann die Reichweite des Elektroautos erheblich vergrößern, ____ man vorausschauend fährt und unnötiges Bremsen vermeidet.
questions.explanation: This is a modal clause answering 'how' something is achieved. 'Indem' is the subordinating conjunction used to describe the method or means.

questions.questionText: Wir werden den Ausflug wie geplant durchführen, ____ es fängt am Morgen wie aus Kübeln an zu regnen.
questions.explanation: 'Es sei denn' means 'unless'. When followed by a clause without 'dass', it unexpectedly maintains standard main clause word order (verb 'fängt' in position 2), which perfectly aligns with the given phrase.

questions.questionText: In Großstädten nutzen immer mehr Menschen das Fahrrad, ____ auf dem Land weiterhin das Auto dominiert.
questions.explanation: 'Wohingegen' is an adversative subordinating conjunction used to contrast two completely opposing realities ('whereas / while on the other hand'). The verb 'dominiert' is pushed to the end.

questions.questionText: Der Patient darf die Klinik auf eigenen Wunsch verlassen, ____ er sich der gesundheitlichen Risiken vollkommen bewusst ist.
questions.explanation: Both 'sofern' and 'vorausgesetzt (dass)' mean 'provided that'. However, 'vorausgesetzt' would require 'dass' here to function as a subordinating conjunction with this exact placement. Therefore, 'sofern' is the correct conditional connector.

questions.questionText: Viele Arbeitnehmer arbeiten auch im Krankheitsfall von zu Hause aus, ____ die Genesung massiv verzögert wird.
questions.explanation: This requires a relative connector representing a whole previous clause statement ('by means of which / as a result of which'). 'Wodurch' introduces this non-personal modal/consecutive effect correctly.

questions.questionText: Ich kann Ihnen diese Investition nicht empfehlen, ____ ich die aktuelle Marktlage für viel zu instabil halte.
questions.explanation: 'Zumal' is an advanced causal subordinating conjunction that means 'especially since / particularly because'. It adds a primary driving reason to a statement and sends the verb 'halte' to the end.

questions.questionText: Er ging zur Arbeit, ____ er starke Kopfschmerzen hatte.
questions.explanation: The sentence expresses contrast — he went to work despite having a headache. 'Obwohl' (although) is the correct subordinating conjunction for concession.

questions.questionText: Die Sitzung wurde verschoben, ____ mehrere Teilnehmer krank waren.
questions.explanation: 'Weil' introduces the reason for postponing the meeting — several participants were ill. 'Weil' is a subordinating conjunction requiring verb-final word order.

questions.questionText: Sie spricht leise, ____ niemand gestört wird.
questions.explanation: 'Damit' (so that / in order that) expresses purpose — she speaks quietly with the intention that no one is disturbed.

questions.questionText: ____ er wenig Erfahrung hatte, bekam er die Stelle.
questions.explanation: The sentence shows contradiction — he got the job despite having little experience. 'Obwohl' introduces the concessive clause.

questions.questionText: Die Straßen waren vereist, ____ viele Unfälle passierten.
questions.explanation: 'Sodass' introduces a consecutive clause expressing result — the icy roads caused many accidents as a consequence.

questions.questionText: ____ die Regierung neue Maßnahmen eingeführt hat, bleibt die Situation schwierig.
questions.explanation: The sentence expresses contrast between new government measures and the continuing difficult situation. 'Obwohl' is the concessive conjunction.

questions.questionText: Er trainiert täglich, ____ seine Leistung kontinuierlich zu verbessern.
questions.explanation: 'Um ... zu' expresses purpose — he trains daily in order to continuously improve his performance.

questions.questionText: Sie blieb ruhig, ____ sie innerlich sehr nervös war.
questions.explanation: 'Obwohl' correctly introduces a contrast — she stayed calm although she was very nervous inside.

questions.questionText: ____ der Zug Verspätung hatte, erreichten wir den Anschluss noch rechtzeitig.
questions.explanation: The sentence contrasts the train delay with still catching the connection in time. 'Obwohl' introduces the concession.

questions.questionText: Die Firma investiert viel Geld in Forschung, ____ wettbewerbsfähig zu bleiben.
questions.explanation: 'Um ... zu' expresses intention or goal — the company invests to remain competitive.

questions.questionText: Er kündigte seinen Job, ____ er noch keine neue Stelle gefunden hatte.
questions.explanation: 'Obwohl' expresses an unexpected contrast — he quit despite not having found a new job yet.

questions.questionText: ____ die Temperaturen weiter steigen, müssen neue Maßnahmen ergriffen werden.
questions.explanation: 'Falls' introduces a conditional clause — if temperatures continue to rise, new measures must be taken.

questions.questionText: Die Präsentation war schlecht vorbereitet, ____ das Publikum schnell das Interesse verlor.
questions.explanation: 'Sodass' introduces the result of the poorly prepared presentation — the audience quickly lost interest.

questions.questionText: ____ er regelmäßig Sport treibt, fühlt er sich oft erschöpft.
questions.explanation: 'Obwohl' expresses a contradiction — despite exercising regularly, he often feels exhausted.

questions.questionText: Sie überprüfte die Daten mehrmals, ____ mögliche Fehler zu vermeiden.
questions.explanation: 'Um ... zu' expresses purpose — she checked the data multiple times in order to avoid possible errors.

questions.questionText: ____ die Nachfrage gestiegen ist, kann das Unternehmen nicht schneller produzieren.
questions.explanation: 'Obwohl' expresses contrast — despite increased demand, the company cannot produce faster.

questions.questionText: Er machte sich Notizen, ____ er später nichts vergessen würde.
questions.explanation: 'Damit' introduces the purpose clause — he made notes so that he wouldn't forget anything later.

questions.questionText: ____ die Experten gewarnt hatten, wurden keine Sicherheitsmaßnahmen getroffen.
questions.explanation: 'Obwohl' shows contradiction — despite expert warnings, no safety measures were taken.

questions.questionText: Die Verhandlungen dauerten länger als erwartet, ____ beide Seiten eine Einigung erzielen wollten.
questions.explanation: 'Weil' gives the reason — the negotiations lasted longer because both sides wanted to reach an agreement.

questions.questionText: ____ er die Unterlagen gründlich gelesen hatte, unterschrieb er den Vertrag.
questions.explanation: 'Nachdem' introduces an action completed before another past action — after reading the documents thoroughly, he signed the contract.

questions.questionText: Er hat lange studiert, ____ hat er die Prüfung nicht bestanden.
questions.explanation: Trotzdem is a conjunctive adverb (position 0 or 1) meaning 'nevertheless'. It contrasts two main clauses. Obwohl would require subordinate clause word order.

questions.questionText: ____ er krank war, kam er zur Arbeit.
questions.explanation: Obwohl introduces a subordinate clause (verb at the end) meaning 'although'.

questions.questionText: Ich helfe dir, ____ du mir später auch hilfst.
questions.explanation: Sofern means 'provided that' and introduces a conditional subordinate clause. It is more formal than 'wenn' for conditions.

questions.questionText: ____ du dich beeilst, wirst du den Zug verpassen.
questions.explanation: Selbst wenn means 'even if' and expresses a strong concession. The main clause is negative (verpassen).

questions.questionText: Sie hat den Job bekommen, ____ sie wenig Berufserfahrung hat.
questions.explanation: Obwohl introduces a subordinate clause (verb at end: hat) meaning 'although'.

questions.questionText: Er ist nicht nur intelligent, ____ auch sehr fleißig.
questions.explanation: Sondern is used after a negative clause (nicht nur) to introduce a contrasting positive addition: 'but rather'.

questions.questionText: Ich möchte Deutsch lernen, ____ ich in Berlin studieren will.
questions.explanation: Denn introduces a main clause (verb position 2) giving a reason. It is more formal than 'weil' in some contexts, but here 'weil' is not an option and 'denn' fits.

questions.questionText: ____ des schlechten Wetters fiel das Picknick aus.
questions.explanation: Wegen is a preposition (not a conjunction) but often tested as a connector. It takes genitive (des Wetters) and means 'because of'.

questions.questionText: Sie arbeitet viel, ____ sie eine Beförderung anstrebt.
questions.explanation: Denn connects two main clauses with a reason. Nämlich would be placed after the subject in the second clause.

questions.questionText: ____ du schon mal in Japan warst, kannst du mir etwas empfehlen?
questions.explanation: Da introduces a subordinate clause with a reason, often when the reason is already known to the listener. It sounds more natural here than 'weil'.

questions.questionText: Er hat das Fenster geöffnet, ____ er frische Luft hereinlassen wollte.
questions.explanation: Denn introduces a main clause explaining the reason (verb position 2: wollte). 'Um' would require 'zu' + infinitive, 'damit' requires subordinate clause with different subject.

questions.questionText: ____ der Chef kommt, verhalten sich alle leiser.
questions.explanation: Wenn is used for repeated or general time (whenever). Als is for a single past event, which doesn't fit here.

questions.questionText: ____ wir angekommen waren, begann das Konzert.
questions.explanation: Nachdem introduces a temporal clause meaning 'after'. The action in the main clause happens after the subordinate clause. Plusquamperfekt (waren angekommen) is typical.

questions.questionText: Du musst dich entscheiden, ____ für das eine ____ für das andere.
questions.explanation: Entweder...oder means 'either...or' and presents two mutually exclusive options.

questions.questionText: ____ des hohen Preises kaufte er das Auto trotzdem.
questions.explanation: Trotz is a preposition requiring genitive (des Preises) meaning 'despite'. Trotzdem is an adverb and cannot take a noun object.

questions.questionText: Ich rufe dich an, ____ ich zu Hause bin.
questions.explanation: Sobald means 'as soon as' and indicates an immediate temporal sequence. The action in the main clause happens right after the subordinate clause.

questions.questionText: ____ du deine Hausaufgaben gemacht hast, darfst du fernsehen.
questions.explanation: Wenn here means 'whenever' or 'if', introducing a condition. Not a single past event, so 'als' is wrong.

questions.questionText: Er ist sehr sportlich, ____ spielt er Tennis und Fußball.
questions.explanation: Nämlich (position after the verb) explains or gives a reason: 'that is to say'. It is placed directly after the verb in the clause.

questions.questionText: Er trat die Reise nicht an, ____ er krank geworden war.
questions.explanation: Denn introduces a main clause (verb position 2: war) explaining the reason. 'Und zwar' specifies, 'nämlich' would need different word order.

questions.questionText: ____ du dich nicht beeilst, verpasst du den Bus.
questions.explanation: Wenn is used for conditional clauses. Falls is more hypothetical, sofern more formal/positive condition. Here 'wenn' is the most natural choice.
